records.claim_text: In SAP Project System the current status of a project object determines which business transactions may be executed on it.
records.evidence_quote: The current status of a project or an object in a project determines which business transactions can be executed.

records.claim_text: PS status management distinguishes two status types: system statuses set by the application and user statuses defined by the customer.
records.evidence_quote: Status management differentiates between system statuses and user statuses.

records.claim_text: Standard SAP performs no authorization check when a user sets a system status on a project object.
records.evidence_quote: SAP does not provide an authorization check for setting system statuses.

records.claim_text: The active system status determines which business transactions can be performed with a work breakdown structure and its WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: The active system status determines which business transactions you can perform with work breakdown structures and WBS elements.

records.claim_text: System statuses cascade downward from project definition to WBS elements and from a WBS element to its subordinate WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: System statuses are passed from the project definition to the WBS elements and from the WBS elements to the subordinate WBS elements.

records.claim_text: The Locked and Final billing system statuses are exceptions and are not inherited down the WBS hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: The system statuses Locked and Final billing are exceptions to this.

records.claim_text: System statuses are cancelled one at a time in reverse order until a status that cannot be cancelled is reached.
records.evidence_quote: You cancel system statuses on by one, until you arrive at a status that cannot be canceled.

records.claim_text: Automatically set system statuses such as Partially released cannot be cancelled by a user.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot cancel system statuses that are set automatically (in the background by the system)

records.claim_text: Cancelling TECO or CLSD on a WBS element also cancels it on the superior WBS element but not on subordinate elements.
records.evidence_quote: If you cancel the statuses Technically completed or Closed , the system automatically cancels this status in the superior WBS element.

records.claim_text: CRTD is the initial WBS element system status; structuring, date planning and cost/revenue planning happen in it.
records.evidence_quote: This is the initial system status for new WBS elements. In this status you structure the project and plan dates, costs and revenues.

records.claim_text: In CRTD a WBS element permits budgeting and assignment of networks that are not yet released.
records.evidence_quote: Allows you to assign networks, which do not yet have Released status

records.claim_text: Release (REL) is the WBS status in which costs and revenues may be assigned and actual costs posted and transferred.
records.evidence_quote: In this status you can assign costs and revenues to WBS elements.

records.claim_text: A WBS element cannot be moved back from Released to Created because actual values from purchase orders or confirmations may exist.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot change the status from Released to Created , as actual values from, for instance, purchase orders or confirmations may have been posted

records.claim_text: TECO marks a WBS element technically complete while further costs are still expected and still postable.
records.evidence_quote: You use this status for WBS elements that are completed from a technical point of view, but where you still expect costs to accrue.

records.claim_text: Setting TECO on a WBS element requires CRTD or REL, and the completion indicator for transfer price agreements.
records.evidence_quote: The Created or Released status must have been set. The completion indicator must be set for transfer price agreements.

records.claim_text: Cancelling TECO on a WBS element returns the element to Released status.
records.evidence_quote: You can cancel the Technically completed status. In this case the system sets the Released status.

records.claim_text: Reopening from TECO can be blocked by defining a user status that prohibits the Revoke technical completion business transaction.
records.evidence_quote: You can prevent the Technically completed status from being canceled. Create a user status that prohibits the Revoke technical completion business transaction.

records.claim_text: CLSD marks a WBS element complete from both a logistical and an accounting point of view.
records.evidence_quote: a work breakdown structure or WBS element that has been completed from both a logistic and an accounting point of view

records.claim_text: CLSD can only be set on a project definition or WBS element that is already Released or Technically completed.
records.evidence_quote: The project definition or the WBS element have either the Released or the Technically completed status.

records.claim_text: CLSD prohibits posting actual costs to the WBS element and prohibits assigning networks, production orders or CO orders to it.
records.evidence_quote: You from assigning networks, production orders or CO orders to the WBS element.

records.claim_text: Under CLSD actual costs may still be posted to orders and networks already assigned to the WBS element if their own status permits.
records.evidence_quote: You to post actual costs to orders and networks that are assigned to the WBS element, as long as their status permit this

records.claim_text: Once CLSD is set no further changes to the project hierarchy are possible, and the status is passed to subordinate WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: In the Closed status you can no longer make any changes to the project hierarchy.

records.claim_text: Setting CLSD deactivates assets under construction assigned to the WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: The status deactivates assets in construction that are assigned to the WBS element.

records.claim_text: Cancelling CLSD on a WBS element sets the status back to Technically completed.
records.evidence_quote: You can cancel the Closed status. In this case the system sets the Technically completed status.

records.claim_text: Deletion flag (DLFL) marks WBS elements logically deleted but not physically deleted, and prohibits all business transactions.
records.evidence_quote: The status is passed on to subordinate WBS elements. It prohibits all business transactions.

records.claim_text: DLFL requires the WBS element be fully settled or settlement-irrelevant, with no commitments and no account-assigned reservations or purchase requisitions.
records.evidence_quote: There are no reservations or purchase requisitions that are account assigned to the WBS element.

records.claim_text: The deletion flag can be cancelled as long as the deletion indicator has not yet been set; DLFL precedes the deletion indicator.
records.evidence_quote: As long you have not set a deletion indicator, you can cancel the Deletion flag status.

records.claim_text: Final billing (FNBL) blocks further billing on a billing WBS element while still allowing cost postings, and is not inherited downward.
records.evidence_quote: With this status you can prevent further billing for this WBS element. However, you can still post costs

records.claim_text: WBS elements support granular locks: DDLK dates, PLLK planning, BMLK budget management, AALK account assignment and MDLK master data.
records.evidence_quote: Budget management locked (BMLK)

records.claim_text: Lock statuses can be combined with any other status except Deletion flag and are not passed to subordinate WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: You can set these statuses in addition to every other status except Deletion flag .

records.claim_text: Master data locked (MDLK) prohibits setting another system status and prohibits changing or extending the project hierarchy.
records.evidence_quote: The Master data locked (MDLK) status prohibits Setting of another system status

records.claim_text: Project hierarchy additions and changes are blocked once MDLK, LKD, CLSD, DLFL or DLT is set on the definition or superior element.
records.evidence_quote: MDLK Master data lockedLKD LockedCLSD ClosedDLFL Deletion flagDLT Deleted

records.claim_text: Adding to the project hierarchy is controlled by business transaction PSEI Expand structure, which the system or user status must allow.
records.evidence_quote: You can add to the project hierarchy if the system or user status allows transaction PSEI Expand structure.

records.claim_text: Changing the project hierarchy is controlled by business transaction PSVE Change structure, which the system or user status must allow.
records.evidence_quote: You can change the project hierarchy if the system or user status allows transaction PSVE Change structure

records.claim_text: A business transaction executes only when at least one status permits it and no status prohibits it.
records.evidence_quote: You can perform a business transaction, if At least one user status or system status permits the transaction

records.claim_text: A status can allow a business transaction, allow it with a warning the user may override, or prohibit it outright.
records.evidence_quote: Allow a business transaction Allow the transaction, but generate a warning Prohibit the transaction

records.claim_text: User statuses supplement system statuses, are never inherited down a hierarchy, and are not copied when a project is copied.
records.evidence_quote: User statuses are not passed on down a hierarchy If you create a project by copying another project, the user status is not copied either.

records.claim_text: User statuses exist only inside a status profile, which must be created per object type and assigned to a project or network profile.
records.evidence_quote: You have to assign a status profile to a project profile or a network profile, before you can use a status profile

records.claim_text: A status profile entry defines short text, status number, initial status, automatic setting, and the business transactions allowed or prohibited.
records.evidence_quote: Business transactions that are allowed or prohibited, if a user status is set

records.claim_text: Only one numbered user status may be active at a time on a WBS or network; unnumbered user statuses can always be set.
records.evidence_quote: only one user status with a status number can be active at one time in a work breakdown structure or network

records.claim_text: Lowest and highest status numbers define which user status must be set first, which may follow, and whether a status can be cancelled.
records.evidence_quote: Whether user statuses can be canceled and if so, which of the previous statuses is set.

records.claim_text: A user status whose lowest and highest numbers are equal to its own number cannot be cancelled, giving a terminal state.
records.evidence_quote: The Valuation status cannot be canceled.

records.claim_text: The status profile on a project object can only be swapped while no user status has yet been set on that object.
records.evidence_quote: You can only change the status profile, if no user status has been set.

records.claim_text: The status detail screen shows active user and system statuses together with the business transactions they allow or prohibit.
records.evidence_quote: an overview of the business transactions that these statuses allow or prohibit

records.claim_text: Statuses are shown both as a four-character abbreviation and as a 30-character text, both language dependent.
records.evidence_quote: 30 character textAs a four character abbreviation

records.claim_text: Network system status flows from network header to activities to activity elements, except Account assignment locked and Locked.
records.evidence_quote: The system status is passed from the network header to the activities and from the activities to the activity elements.

records.claim_text: A network or activity in CRTD prohibits posting actual costs but allows physical deletion of activities and activity elements.
records.evidence_quote: Allows you to directly (physically) delete activities and activity elementsProhibits you from posting actual costs

records.claim_text: Released network status is the precondition for posting actual costs and allows creating reservations or purchase requisitions for components.
records.evidence_quote: Allows you to create reservations or purchase requisitions for all components, depending on settings elsewhere.

records.claim_text: The Released status on a network cannot be cancelled.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot cancel the Released status.

records.claim_text: TECO on a network deletes purchase requisitions and requirements for material components and sets deletion flags on those components.
records.evidence_quote: Deletes purchase requisitions and requirements for material components, if any exist.

records.claim_text: TECO on a network still allows actual postings such as confirmations but prevents setting a user status.
records.evidence_quote: Prevents you setting a user status

records.claim_text: Cancelling TECO on a network header does not automatically cancel it on the activities and activity elements.
records.evidence_quote: If you cancel the Technically completed status in the network header, the status is not automatically canceled in the activities

records.claim_text: Closing a network requires no balance and confirmation of all activities that require confirmation.
records.evidence_quote: No balance existsAll activities that require confirmation have been confirmed.

records.claim_text: Closing a network prevents actual postings such as confirmations, and cancelling it restores the previous Released or TECO status.
records.evidence_quote: You can cancel the Closed status. The system then set the previous status (

records.claim_text: Account assignment locked can be set on a network header or on an activity depending on network type, blocking account assignment.
records.evidence_quote: Depending on the network type, you can set the Account assignment locked status either only in the network header or only in the activity

records.claim_text: Locked (LKD) can only be set on the network header and is passed to all activities.
records.evidence_quote: You can only set the Locked status in the network header. The status is passed on to all activities.

records.claim_text: Releasing a network releases all its activities, activity elements and production resources/tools.
records.evidence_quote: When you release a network, all activities, activity elements and production resources/tools are also released.

records.claim_text: Releasing individual activities sets Partially released on the network header; an activity may only be released if its WBS element is PREL or REL.
records.evidence_quote: You can only release an activity which is assigned to a WBS element if the WBS element has the status Partially released or Released

records.claim_text: Standard WBS elements have no own status; the standard project definition status applies to all of them and TECO does not exist.
records.evidence_quote: Standard WBS elements do not have their own status. The status of the standard project definition is valid for all WBS elements.

records.claim_text: The Budgeted system status is set on first budget allocation, persists after budget removal, and blocks deletion and reassignment of WBS elements.
records.evidence_quote: After you allocate budget to a WBS element for the first time, the system status budgeted is set.

records.claim_text: The Budgeted status can be removed only for WBS elements with budget zero using the Remove Budgeted Status tool.
records.evidence_quote: You can remove the budgeted system status for WBS elements with budget 0.

records.claim_text: Availability control being active is itself visible as a system status on the budget-carrying WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: The Availability control activated system status is set for the WBS element budget object.

records.claim_text: PS creates a project version automatically whenever a system and/or user status changes on selected objects, giving a status history.
records.evidence_quote: The system automatically creates a project version when there is a system and/or user status change in the selected objects.

records.claim_text: Which system or user statuses trigger creation of a project version is defined in Project System customizing.
records.evidence_quote: You define the user/system statuses which trigger creation of project versions in Project System customizing.

records.claim_text: Project versions are point-in-time snapshots that document the past state of the project as a history for comparison.
records.evidence_quote: Document (as a history) the state of the project in the past

records.claim_text: Change authorization in PS is enforced through named authorization objects including C_PROJ_VNR, C_PROJ_KOK, C_PROJ_TCD, C_PRPS_KOK, C_PRPS_USR and C_PRPS_VNR.
records.evidence_quote: C_PROJ_VNR Project manager for project definition

records.claim_text: WBS-level authorization objects include C_PRPS_ART project types, C_PRPS_KOK controlling area, C_PRPS_KST cost center and C_PRPS_PRC profit center.
records.evidence_quote: C_PRPS_KOK Controlling area for WBS element

records.claim_text: PS change authorization is checked with activity 02 change or transaction type V change on the relevant authorization objects.
records.evidence_quote: (activity 02: change, or transaction type V: change)

records.claim_text: Setting the deletion flag requires PS change authorization for project definitions, WBS elements and networks.
records.evidence_quote: you must have authorization to make changes in the Project System for project definitions, WBS elements, and networks

records.claim_text: Object-Based Authorization gives per-object user access control for project definition, WBS, network, activity and activity element in PS.
records.evidence_quote: The Object-Based Authorization (OBA) function allows easy control of user-access to individual project objects for selected use cases and transactions in Project System (PS).

records.claim_text: OBA supports READ (1), WRITE (2), WRITE+CREATE, ADMIN (3) and NO AUTH (4), with No Authorization taking highest precedence.
records.evidence_quote: The highest-priority authorization type, whether it is for a user or user-group, takes precedence during an authorization check.

records.claim_text: OBA must be switched on via a flag in the project profile or network profile and requires migration report RPSOBA_MIGRATE for running projects.
records.evidence_quote: To use this function, you must activate it in the project profile or network profile.

records.claim_text: OBA does not replace role-based authorization; classic PFCG authorizations are still required to reach the project objects.
records.evidence_quote: In addition to the OBA authorizations, you must have the necessary PFCG authorizations, in order to have access to the project objects.

records.claim_text: OBA authorizations are inherited to lower-level objects as non-modifiable entries, but can be overridden by a local higher-priority assignment.
records.evidence_quote: The system automatically passes on authorizations to lower-level objects. These inherited authorizations are non-modifiable.

records.claim_text: A user cannot change the OBA authorizations granted to their own user or to a user group they belong to.
records.evidence_quote: You cannot change the authorizations granted to your user. This also holds good for the authorizations granted via a user group.

records.claim_text: In S/4HANA Cloud enterprise projects a processing status expresses the lifecycle phase and controls which processing steps are allowed.
records.evidence_quote: The processing status of an enterprise project or WBS element indicates what part of the project lifecycle the project or WBS element is in.

records.claim_text: Cloud enterprise projects keep a separate finer-grained system status alongside the coarse processing status shown to users.
records.evidence_quote: Projects and WBS elements also have a system status which is related to their processing status

records.claim_text: Partially Released cannot be set manually; it is derived automatically when any lower-level WBS element is set to Released.
records.evidence_quote: This status cannot be set manually. It is set automatically when any of the lower-level WBS elements are set to Released.

records.claim_text: Release is the gate for posting commitments or actual costs to a Cloud project or WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: Once a project or WBS element has been released, you can post commitments or actual costs to it.

records.claim_text: Completed freezes structure, dates, status and responsibilities editing but still permits posting further costs.
records.evidence_quote: You can no longer edit the project or WBS element data such as work breakdown structure, dates, status or responsibilities.

records.claim_text: A Cloud project can be moved back from Completed to Released and from Closed to Completed.
records.evidence_quote: You have the option to move the project or WBS element back to the Completed status.

records.claim_text: Locked can be applied to any Cloud processing status except Closed and makes the project or WBS element non-editable until unlocked.
records.evidence_quote: A project or WBS element with the status Locked cannot be edited.

records.claim_text: For a Created Cloud project a maintenance or production order may be created but cannot be released.
records.evidence_quote: Allowed to create but cannot release the order

records.claim_text: Billing documents can be generated against a Created-status WBS element but cannot be posted.
records.evidence_quote: Billing document can be generated when WBS is in Created status; however, you cannot post them.

records.claim_text: The Cloud lifecycle permission matrix is rendered with tick/cross glyph images, so individual cell values cannot be quoted as text.
records.evidence_quote: The following table shows the operation that can be performed during various stages of the project lifecycle.

records.claim_text: ProcessingStatus fixed value 00 is Created in enterprise projects and In Planning in professional services projects.
records.evidence_quote: 00 Created In Planning

records.claim_text: ProcessingStatus fixed value 10 is Released in enterprise projects and In Execution in professional services projects.
records.evidence_quote: 10 Released In Execution

records.claim_text: ProcessingStatus fixed value 12 is Partially Released and 20 is Locked, both applicable only to enterprise projects.
records.evidence_quote: 12 Partially Released –– (not applicable)

records.claim_text: ProcessingStatus fixed value 40 is Completed and 42 is Closed in both enterprise and professional services projects.
records.evidence_quote: 42 Closed Closed

records.claim_text: CDS view I_EntProjProcessingStatus is the released code list of supported ProcessingStatus values for enterprise projects.
records.evidence_quote: This CDS view provides supported values for ProcessingStatus.

records.claim_text: Enterprise project WBS element status changes are made by POSTing the ChangeEntProjElmntProcgStatus function import keyed by ProjectElementUUID.
records.evidence_quote: To set the processing status for a project element, you use the http method POST to call the ChangeEntProjElmntProcgStatus function import.

records.claim_text: The element-level processing status API applies to WBS elements only and is not supported for the enterprise project definition.
records.evidence_quote: This operation is relevant for WBS elements of enterprise projects only. It is currently not supported for the project definition of enterprise projects.

records.claim_text: Project definition processing status is changed by POSTing ChangeEntProjProcgStatus keyed by ProjectUUID, for enterprise and professional services projects.
records.evidence_quote: To set the processing status, you use the http method POST to call the ChangeEntProjProcgStatus function import.

records.claim_text: Inbound OData service ENTPROJECTPROCESSINGSTATUS exposes the processing status code list and its descriptions for enterprise projects.
records.evidence_quote: This inbound OData service enables you to read the processing status code list for enterprise projects and professional services projects

records.claim_text: On-premise PS exposes WBS element system status changes as POST actions on the WorkBreakdownStructureElement entity of api_project_v3.
records.evidence_quote: Perform actions on the WorkBreakdownStructureElement entity to change the System Status of a WBS Element, by using the method POST.

records.claim_text: ReleaseWBSElement is the API action that moves a WBS element system status to released.
records.evidence_quote: Perform the ReleaseWBSElement action on the WorkBreakdownStructureElement entity to change the system status of a WBS Element to released.

records.claim_text: WBS status actions include CompleteWBSElementTechnically, UndoCompleteWBSElementTechly, SetWBSElementToClosed, UndoWBSElementClosed, SetWBSElementToDeletion and UndoWBSElementDeletion.
records.evidence_quote: SAP__self.SetWBSElementToClosed

records.claim_text: Separate API actions lock and unlock WBS element master data, dates, planning, budget, account assignment, or everything at once.
records.evidence_quote: Perform the LockWBSElementAcctAsgt action on the WorkBreakdownStructureElement entity to lock the account assignment of a WBS Element.

records.claim_text: User statuses can be set or reverted on a WBS element via API, optionally passing the status down to lower-level objects.
records.evidence_quote: SAP__self.SetAndPassUserStsToWBSElement

records.claim_text: Project-level API actions include ReleaseProject, CompleteProjectTechnically, UndoCompleteProjectTechnically, SetProjectToClosed, UndoProjectClosed, SetProjectToDeletion and UndoProjectDeletion.
records.evidence_quote: Perform the UndoCompleteProjectTechnically action on the project entity to undo technically completed status of a project.

records.claim_text: Reading WBS element status returns StatusCode, StatusObject, StatusProfile, StatusIsActive, IsUserStatus, StatusShortName and StatusName per status row.
records.evidence_quote: "StatusCode": "I0001", "StatusObject": "PR00000106", "StatusProfile": "", "StatusIsActive": "", "IsUserStatus": "", "StatusShortName": "CRTD"

records.claim_text: Network and activity status actions include ReleaseProjectNetwork, CompleteProjNtwkTechnically, SetProjectNetworkToClosed and their Revert counterparts.
records.evidence_quote: Execute action on the Project to set the Project Network status using the HTTP method POST.

records.claim_text: A dedicated Change WBS Element Status app lets the Project Financial Controller change both system and user status of a WBS element.
records.evidence_quote: With this app, you can change the system and user status of a work breakdown structure element.

records.claim_text: Before cascading a user status to all sub-objects the user is shown an inheritance summary of the affected lower-level objects.
records.evidence_quote: analyze the inheritance summary for all lower level objects

records.claim_text: The WBS status change app runs on OData service PS_WBSELEMENTSTATUSCHANGE_SRV with UI5 application PS_WBSSTA_CHGS1.
records.evidence_quote: OData Service (Version Number) PS_WBSELEMENTSTATUSCHANGE_SRV (1)

records.claim_text: Changing network activity system and user status is a Project Logistics Controller task in a separate dedicated app.
records.evidence_quote: With this app you can change the system and user status of a network activity. This app is available for the role Project Logistics Controller.

records.claim_text: Setting the deletion flag is normally performed by the holder of project authorization, such as the project manager, not the administrator.
records.evidence_quote: The person with project authorization usually sets the status deletion flag .

records.claim_text: An object flagged for deletion cannot be changed, though the flag itself may be removed until the deletion indicator is set.
records.evidence_quote: A network or work breakdown structure that is marked for deletion cannot be changed.

records.claim_text: Deletion-flagged networks, activities and orders distort project reporting, period-end closing and progress determination.
records.evidence_quote: Project objects or assignments to projects that have deletion flags can lead to inaccuracies in some applications or functions.

records.claim_text: Every business transaction belongs to a transaction group used by availability control to apply per-group budget tolerance limits.
records.evidence_quote: All business transactions are assigned to a transaction group in availability control.

records.claim_text: SAP training states a user status must always be defined inside a status profile created for an object type in Customizing.
records.evidence_quote: You must always define a user status within a status profile.

records.claim_text: SAP training frames statuses as serving documentation, selection criteria for reporting, and permitting or prohibiting business transactions.
records.evidence_quote: Statuses are used for documentation, selection criteria, and to permit or prohibit business transactions.

records.claim_text: SAP training confirms system statuses are delivered by SAP to control primary business activities and cannot be changed by customers.
records.evidence_quote: System statuses have been set up by the SAP system to control primary business activities. You cannot change them.

records.claim_text: The status profile is one of the general settings carried on the project profile that defaults into objects created from it.
records.evidence_quote: general settings including field key and status profile

records.claim_text: SAP PS documentation exposes no dedicated status change-document or status audit-log topic; project versions are the documented status history.
records.evidence_quote: Project versions are: Time-dependent Status-dependent

records.claim_text: System statuses are set by selecting WBS elements or the project definition and choosing the status from the Edit Status menu.
records.evidence_quote: Select the WBS elements for which you want to set a system status or call up the project definition.
